Package org.saidone.protoalf.platform

package org.saidone.protoalf.platform
Adapts Alfresco repository services to authenticated gRPC operations.

Service boundaries

Each Grpc<Service> corresponds to an Alfresco service: node metadata, file/folder operations, content, version history, search, dictionary lookups, the trashcan (archive store) and credential authentication. Protobuf messages replace local repository objects. Aggregate node snapshots and updates, materialized content access and streaming transfers are documented remote extensions rather than implementations of Alfresco Java interfaces.

Authentication and transactions

TicketInterceptor requires an alfresco-ticket header on every operation except credential authentication. It records the validated username in the gRPC context; repository callbacks run as that user. Both ticket validation and repository execution restore the previous Alfresco thread authentication. Read operations use read-only transactions and mutations use retryable read-write transactions. Unary responses are emitted only after the transaction succeeds.

Downloads resolve their content reader inside a transaction, then stream bytes outside it so a retry cannot duplicate output. Uploads spool their input before creating a document. The transactional write reopens the spool for every attempt, and temporary files are cleaned up on completion, cancellation and failure.

References and values

Node arguments accept a full repository reference, a bare workspace node ID, or -root-, -my- and -shared-. Aliases resolve as the caller. Qualified property, aspect and type names accept prefix:localName or expanded {namespace-uri}localName notation. Read snapshots preserve supported scalar types, collection cardinality and null markers, while exposing content metadata without content-store URLs. Write inputs use the same typed properties, with explicit scalar/list cardinality validated against dictionary definitions.

Failure delivery

RPC failures are sent to response observers using gRPC statuses; they are not declared as synchronous exceptions on service method signatures. Shared repository error translation uses these mappings:

Repository failures and their transport status
ConditionStatus
Missing/invalid ticket or rejected credentialsUNAUTHENTICATED
Repository permission deniedPERMISSION_DENIED
Unresolved or missing node/modelNOT_FOUND
Duplicate child nameALREADY_EXISTS
Lock or repository integrity constraintFAILED_PRECONDITION
Invalid input or cyclic folder operationINVALID_ARGUMENT
Unexpected repository failureINTERNAL

Explicit status exceptions keep their status. Content extraction and streaming add operation-specific statuses described on the corresponding methods. Internal exception details are omitted from permission and unexpected-failure responses, while diagnostic causes remain available in server logs.
